sections.h2: Why is Union County called the Top of Georgia?
sections.html:
Brasstown Bald, the highest mountain in Georgia, rises in the southeast corner of Union County and straddles the Towns County line. That is why locals call the county the Top of Georgia. The county measures 329.02 square miles, with 322.55 of them land, and Blairsville is the seat.

Union was carved from Cherokee County territory in the Georgia Land Lottery of 1832, after gold found in the 1820s made land long held by Native Americans more attractive to settlers. The county history page says the name probably traces to the Union Party, not to the Civil War, which came nearly thirty years later. Residents live in Blairsville, in the community of Suches, or out in the countryside among pastures and creeks.

For a seller, that mix means very different parcels: a mountain cabin with a view, a lot in town, or acreage with road frontage. Each needs its own approach to pricing, access and, above all, a clean tax record before closing.

sections.h2: How does the Union County housing market look in Census data?
sections.html:
Union has grown quickly. The Census Bureau puts the July 2025 population at 27,859, which is 13.1% above the 2020 count of 24,632. Owners occupy 84.4% of housing units, and the middle home value for 2020 to 2024 is $307,400.

More than a third of residents are 65 or older, and the average household has 2.24 people. Many homes here belong to retirees and second-home owners, and 264 building permits in 2025 show steady new construction. Estates and out-of-area owners are a regular source of listings.

sections.h2: Which Union County office handles what?
sections.html:
Billing and valuing are split, and the two offices are not interchangeable. The tax commissioner's site says the office bills, collects and disburses taxes; the assessors decide value.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 439-6017, in the courthouse at 65 Courthouse Street, Blairsville, for bills, payments and tag and title work.
  • Tax assessors: (706) 439-6011, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., for values, returns, homestead applications and exemptions.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds, and copies of your warranty deed.

The assessors' page states that five real-property appraisers, one personal property appraiser and a clerk keep the parcel records. It also carries a public notice that the county hired Georgia Mass Appraisal Solutions and Services to help revalue homes, commercial, industrial and farm parcels. Appraisers drive vehicles with a Union County seal and do not enter residences or buildings.

sections.h2: When are Union County property taxes due, and what do late bills cost?
sections.html:
The county tax site says real estate and business personal property taxes are due by December 20 of each year. Mobile and modular home tax is due April 1, and motor vehicles follow the owner's birthday. Boat tax shares the December 20 date, with assessment notices mailed in May.

Once the date passes, 1% interest is added each month on the amount due, and a bill that stays unpaid for 90 days can have a tax lien, called a FIFA, recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. The county warns that such records are public and credit bureaus can see them. After 90 days of delinquency the tax office may also begin tax sale proceedings.

  • Taxpayers get at least 60 days to pay the annual bill.
  • Failing to receive a bill does not excuse payment.
  • The City of Blairsville bills and collects its own property tax.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Union County assessment?
sections.html:
Assessment notices go out in May, and you have 45 days from the notice date to challenge the value. File with the Board of Assessors, and if the two sides cannot agree, the appeal moves on to the Board of Equalization, a panel the Grand Jury appoints. After that decision you may continue to Superior Court by filing a written notice with the assessors.

Georgia also lets some owners choose arbitration or a certified hearing officer instead of the board, and you make that choice when you file. Mobile and modular home owners get two chances: one during the return period and another within 45 days after the bill is mailed, which the county says usually happens in mid February.

Not filing a required return can bring a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest. Returns for real estate are due between January 1 and April 1 where property has changed or been acquired.

sections.h2: How do I get homestead relief in Union County?
sections.html:
Bring a copy of your warranty deed to the Tax Assessor's office and apply by April 1. You must own and occupy the house on January 1, and once approved, the exemption stays in place until you move or your deed changes. A late application is activated the next year.

The county's tax site says Union offers local homestead exemptions that beat the state's, while the state revenue department's county page lists none, so ask the assessors for current figures before you rely on either. Freeport exemption covers business inventory, and current-use programs for farm and forest land require staying undeveloped, with stiff penalties for breaking the commitment.

sections.h2: How should I handle taxes when I sell in Union County?
sections.html:
Tax bills go to the owner of record on January 1, so a buyer who closes in March or September will not get that year's bill from the county. Plan for the closing agent to pay it from your proceeds, and ask the tax office for a current payoff in writing.

The county site explains that a new owner will not receive a bill for the year of purchase, which is why a prorated payment on the settlement statement is worth checking line by line. If the house is a mountain rental or a cabin left by a relative, ask about every year it was held. Selling to a cash buyer can wrap up the payoff and the deed recording in one visit to the courthouse.

faqs.q: What is the Union County property tax due date?
faqs.a: December 20 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and modular homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: What interest applies after the Union County deadline?
faqs.a: The tax site states 1% interest each month on the amount due. A lien can be filed after 90 days unpaid.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Union County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. The appeal goes to the Board of Assessors first and then to the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Does Union County have a late homestead filing option?
faqs.a: An application received after April 1 is not applied to that year. The assessors activate it the following year.

faqs.q: Who bills Blairsville city property tax?
faqs.a: The City of Blairsville bills and collects its own portion. The county tax commissioner handles county and school bills.
